clue.text: Injury caused by birch tree catching lumberjack's head

indicators.note: the birch and the tree together grab and hold a letter between them

parts.note: to birch someone is to flog them with a rod

indicators.note: a head is the top or front, so only the opening letter of the woodsman's word is used

parts.note: opening letter of the woodsman
the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: A woodsman is hurt when a falling birch lands on his head.
explanation.walkthrough: Birch is not the tree here but the verb meaning to flog; the actual tree comes next.
explanation.definitionFit: Whiplash is a neck injury from a sudden jolting movement, typically in car collisions.

clue.text: Cover small cooking vessel

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small
a pan is a pot used for cooking

explanation.surface: An instruction to put a lid on a little saucepan.
explanation.definitionFit: To span is to extend across or stretch over a distance, as a bridge does.

clue.text: Something black and brown — that's checked

definitions.note: a noun phrase: something with a checked pattern

parts.note: tar is a black sticky substance
tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: Describing a fabric pattern of black and brown squares.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartan is the woollen cloth woven in a pattern of crossing coloured stripes forming squares, associated with Scottish clans.

clue.text: Unmixed, last of ginger beer stirred into dessert

indicators.note: the earlier letters go inside the pudding word

parts.note: pud is British slang for pudding, a dessert

indicators.note: a drink that is stirred has its contents mixed about, so the letters move
only the final letter of the spice word is wanted

parts.note: final letter of ginger
taken as written

explanation.surface: A recipe step: pour ginger beer into a pudding and stir.
explanation.walkthrough: The R and the rearranged beer both sit between the U and D of the dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A purebred animal comes from parents of one breed, with no crossing of different strains.

clue.text: Terrible milliner: give voice about that

indicators.note: the singing goes around, surrounding the hat maker mentioned as that

parts.note: to give voice is to sing
a milliner makes hats; 'that' points back to this word

explanation.surface: A dreadful hat maker is urged to sing about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' refers back to the milliner, so the hat maker is what the singing goes round.
explanation.definitionFit: Shattering is informal for devastating or exhausting, so it works as an intensely bad, terrible adjective.

clue.text: Shoe: edge held by boy

indicators.note: something held by another is gripped inside it, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: a son is a boy child
a lip is the rim or edge of something

explanation.surface: A shoe whose rim is gripped by a small boy.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip-on is footwear without laces that you simply push your foot into.

clue.text: Member of religious body gentleman put down

parts.note: chap is informal British for a man
past participle of lay, as in laid down to rest

explanation.surface: A churchman is described as a gentleman who was humiliated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put down' suggests insulted, but it means lain, placed lying down.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplain is a clergyman attached to an institution such as a school, hospital or regiment.

clue.text: Dry rolls glazed with egg, superlatively enjoyable

indicators.note: a glaze coats the outside, so the egg word wraps around

parts.note: a nit is the egg of a louse

indicators.note: something that rolls turns over, so the word for dry is read backwards

parts.note: sec is the wine term for dry

explanation.surface: Bread rolls brushed with egg wash taste best of all.
explanation.walkthrough: Rolls and glazed with egg read like baking, but rolls is a verb; NI(CES)T.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of nice, meaning pleasant, is the most pleasing or agreeable.

clue.text: Wicked not having cavities, did you say?

indicators.note: asking what was said points to a word heard rather than seen in print

parts.note: without holes, if that coinage existed

explanation.surface: A playful question whether wickedness means having no holes.
explanation.definitionFit: Unholy means sinful or impious, opposed to what is sacred or godly.

clue.text: Wheel bites when rotated

indicators.note: turning round makes the word face the other way, read right to left

parts.note: nips are little bites

explanation.surface: A wheel that pinches when it is turned.
explanation.definitionFit: To wheel is to turn round rapidly, to whirl or rotate on the spot.

clue.text: Take cut: receipt doctored, paper printed out

indicators.note: a doctored document has been tampered with, so its letters are altered in order
cutting the word short trims off its final letter

parts.note: taken as written, before its tail is cut
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone skims money by falsifying a receipt.
explanation.walkthrough: Take loses its E to give TAK, which is jumbled with receipt.
explanation.definitionFit: Ticker tape was the paper strip on which telegraph machines printed stock prices.

clue.text: Couple of beers for French trip

definitions.note: trip in the sense of a dance step

wordplay.note: two cans of beer, a can being one beer

explanation.surface: Having two beers on a trip to France.
explanation.definitionFit: The cancan is a high-kicking dance from Paris music halls, and to trip is to dance nimbly.

clue.text: One's lifted when facing two animals

parts.note: first animal: a chirping insect
second animal: a flying mammal

explanation.surface: Something gets picked up when confronted by a pair of creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batsman facing is the one receiving the bowling, and raises his bat to play.
explanation.definitionFit: Facing describes a batsman at the crease to receive the ball, and he lifts this wooden implement.

clue.text: Rogue gets near officer

indicators.note: a rogue behaves wildly and out of order, so the letters break out of place

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A villain closes in on a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sergeant is a non-commissioned army rank or police rank above constable.

clue.text: Musical party style

parts.note: Hair is the 1960s rock musical
a do is an informal party

explanation.surface: A fashionable approach to a party with music.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairdo is the way someone's hair is cut and arranged, a coiffure.

clue.text: Fine lace tied in knots

indicators.note: knotted things are tangled up, so the letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Delicate lacework fastened in knots.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine and delicate both describe something thin, dainty and easily damaged.

clue.text: Commercial break some way off

parts.note: an ad is a commercial, an advertisement
a rift is a break or split

explanation.surface: A television ad break that seems distant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commercial break' looks like one phrase, but each word supplies its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Adrift means off course or astray, as in falling some distance short of a target.

clue.text: Trains on time, household items transported in one?

parts.note: to train someone is to teach them
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Railway trains run punctually while carrying people's belongings.
explanation.walkthrough: Trains is a verb, not railway carriages; the definition is a cryptic hint at moving house.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea chest is a large wooden box once used to ship tea and later for packing belongings when moving.

clue.text: A vote beginning to offend God

parts.note: taken as written
a poll is a vote

indicators.note: only the start, the first letter, of the following word is used

parts.note: first letter of offend

explanation.surface: A ballot that might start to upset the Almighty.
explanation.definitionFit: Apollo was the Greek and Roman deity of music, poetry and the sun.

clue.text: Support mates after revolution, encouraging strike

parts.note: to back is to support

indicators.note: a revolution turns something right round, so the word for friends is read backwards

parts.note: mates and pals are friends

explanation.surface: Workers backing comrades in an industrial strike after an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' sounds like industrial action but is a hit, a pat on the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A backslap is a hearty pat on someone's back to congratulate or encourage them.

clue.text: Well-built woman, great South American runner?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a tall strong woman, after the female warriors of Greek myth
second meaning: the huge river, since a river runs

explanation.walkthrough: Runner suggests an athlete, but a river runs, so the great runner is a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a strong warrior woman of legend and the mighty river crossing Brazil.

clue.text: Dance identified, one's pieced together

parts.note: a jig is a lively dance
saw, as in spotted or recognised

explanation.surface: A dance is recognised as something assembled from parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A jigsaw puzzle is made of interlocking cut shapes fitted back into a picture.

clue.text: Top lower

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a knitted pullover garment
second meaning: one that lows, a cow of the Channel Island breed

explanation.walkthrough: Top and lower look like opposites; lower is really something that moos.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a woollen sweater worn on the upper body and a breed of dairy cattle, which moo.

clue.text: Discriminating fact

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a detail or item of information

explanation.definitionFit: The word means choosy as an adjective, and as a noun one detail, as in full particulars.

clue.text: Children's author had tea with Orwell, finally

indicators.note: applied to each word before it, keeping only the closing letter of every one

parts.note: last letters of four words

explanation.surface: One writer took afternoon tea with George Orwell at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' looks as if it applies only to Orwell, but it takes the last letter of every word.
explanation.definitionFit: Roald Dahl wrote much-loved books for young readers such as Matilda and The BFG.

clue.text: Rollers died on the rocks

parts.note: d is the abbreviation for died
a drink on the rocks is served over ice

explanation.surface: Gamblers' fortunes perished when things went wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Dice are the small cubes thrown in games, so they are things that get rolled.

clue.text: Shopping centre inspiring Australian maestro

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the shopping place takes the next word inside

parts.note: a mart is a market
Oz is slang for Australia

explanation.surface: A mall motivates an Australian conductor.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozart, the Austrian composer, is the great classical master of music.

clue.text: Dull, remaining actors

parts.note: left over means remaining
a cast is the set of actors in a play

explanation.surface: Uninspiring performers still left on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Overcast describes cloudy grey weather, a dull sky.
